title: Admission-gradient and prefetch de-escalation to prevent queue cascades during GPU capacity pressure
creator: Aisha Patel
description: After the 2026-03-02 hosted GPU exhaustion incident, we observed cascading queue amplification when many long-running requests flooded specific GPU pools. This ticket implements a set of complementary mitigations: 1) an admission gradient that progressively sheds lower-priority requests based on queue growth signals, 2) a prefetch/deferred-execution de-escalation that limits speculative work during pressure, and 3) telemetry hooks to track admission hysteresis and false-shed rates. Goal: reduce peak queue depth and tail latency without dropping critical P0 traffic.
analysis_summary: Root cause: admission decisions were binary (accept/reject) and prefetch workers continued to spawn speculative batches even as queues grew, amplifying GPU memory and scheduling pressure. Trigger pattern: several mid-sized customers launched high concurrency generation with long context lengths causing KV cache growth and longer token runtimes; autoscaler didn't prime fast enough due to conservative hysteresis.
design_decisions: Use a 3-stage admission gradient (green/yellow/red) with resource-aware thresholds tied to effective_tokens_in_flight metric
Prioritize requests by priority class and estimated token budget (from profiling heuristics) before admission scoring
Limit speculative prefetch/spawn rate proportional to observed queue growth; implement backoff doubling on repeated requeue
Expose soft-shed metrics and control knobs in Console for on-call tuning
action_items: Implement admission-gradient module in router service (ENG-99777-1)
Add prefetch de-escalation toggles and backoff logic to worker pool (ENG-99777-2)
Instrument effective_tokens_in_flight and publish to telemetry (ENG-99777-3)
Create a Console chart and alert for soft-shed-rate and false-shed-rate (ENG-99777-4)
Run canary rollout with synthetic queue pressure scenarios and validate tail-latency improvement (ENG-99777-5)
acceptance_criteria: Under synthetic pressure test (50% higher concurrent long-context requests), 95th token latency reduced by >=25% compared to baseline
Peak GPU queue depth reduced by >=30% without increasing overall request rejection of P0 customers
Soft-shed rate documented and visible in Console; on-call can toggle knob to adjust hysteresis
No user-visible increased 5xx rates in the canary region during 48h observation
implementation_notes: Router config will add weighted admission scoring combining priority, estimated token cost, and pool saturation. Backoff uses exponential multiplier with jitter. We'll add a feature flag with rollout via console rollouts.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-aggressive soft-shed may reject latency-sensitive mid-tier traffic — mitigation: preserve strict headroom for P0 tokens and run A/B traffic splits
Risk: Telemetry sparsity — mitigation: instrument at multiple points (ingress, scheduler, worker) and add dashboards before rollout
Risk: Autoscaler interaction — mitigation: test with autoscaler hysteresis disabled and with production config to tune thresholds
